answers.answer: In 3 players, the tied leaders gain no coin; the unique last player pays 1 coin. In 2 players, the unique leader gains 1 coin and the last player never pays.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: tied lead gives no coin; unique last pays; in a 2-player game the last player never pays.

answers.answer: No. Draw up to the allowance, limited by free Market spaces, so at most two here. Market Followers not drawn remain between rounds and occupy capacity.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers: draw any number up to allowance, limited by free Market spaces; unused Market Followers remain and occupy capacity.

answers.answer: You may fill an action over multiple rounds, but cannot activate it until all required spaces are occupied by Followers or legal Technology (Town Hall needs one of two). A fully activated action may be saved. After execution, ordinary-action Followers return to your bag; Technology remains on its space.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Planning and Actions.

answers.answer: Starting with Start Player, players go clockwise repeatedly, taking one activated action or passing. Passing ends your participation for that Action Phase; you cannot act again, and unused activations retain their Followers on the board for future rounds.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions.

answers.answer: Farm House recruits a Farmer into your bag, advances the Farmers Track one space, and gives the good depicted at that space.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Farm House.

answers.answer: Village recruits one of a Boatman, Craftsman, or Trader into your bag and advances that profession's track. Boatman gives depicted coins (or a Citizen to the first at the last space); Craftsman gives a Technology tile, usable only after you pass; Trader gives a Place Tile, category I on the first advance and I or II on later advances.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment.

answers.answer: No: a newly acquired Technology can be used only after you pass, so it cannot help another action this round after that pass. Your first Technology must replace a Farmer. Later Technologies may replace any profession except Monk; never more than one Technology per Place, none at a one-Follower Place, and Technology cannot be moved.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Craftsman; Technology.

answers.answer: No. The first Traders Track advance permits category I only; each later advance permits I or II. Players may inspect the stacks at any time.
answers.evidence: Setup step 3; Village recruitment — Trader.

answers.answer: University recruits a Scholar into your bag, advances Scholars one space, and gains its depicted Development Points. Castle recruits a Knight into your bag and advances Knights; the fourth Knight leaves draw allowance at 7, and its Citizen goes to the first player there. Monastery recruits a Monk into your bag with no extra track reward. You cannot take the corresponding action again once its track is at its last space.
answers.evidence: Actions table; Castle rewards; Character-track limits.

answers.answer: Yes, a Monk may replace a Knight for an ordinary action. No Knight or Technology can replace a required Monk. No Monk or other substitution can replace the exact profession required on a Beneficial Deed.
answers.evidence: Monks; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Ship moves the Merchant one adjacent town along one Waterway; Wagon moves one adjacent town along one Road. You may take at most one good from that connection, choosing one if there are multiple. Empty connections are legal and yield no good.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods.

answers.answer: Guildhall builds one Trading Station in the Merchant's current town. A town with any player's station cannot receive another, except Orléans, where each player may build one.
answers.evidence: Building.

answers.answer: Scriptorium gains 1 Development Point (move one space on the Development Track). Moving onto or past a coin space collects its depicted coins; the first player onto/past a Citizen space collects that Citizen; reaching/passing a Development Status space immediately changes Status to its shown value.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium; Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Town Hall works with one or two eligible neutral Followers; starting marked Followers cannot be used. Send one or both permanently to free Deed spaces matching their exact professions, possibly on different Deeds. Each placement earns its depicted 1, 2, or 3 coins; Canalization gives a choice of 1 coin or 1 Development Point. The player filling a Deed's last space takes its Citizen.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: Pilgrimage forbids Monk recruitment in that round's Action Phase; it applies before the Event Phase. Other events resolve in Phase 6. The setup stacks Pilgrimage on top, so it opens the game.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass; Setup step 4; Events — Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Food is grain, cheese, or wine; wool is not food. Pay one food good to the Goods Market. If unable to pay food, pay 5 coins; if unable to pay those coins, undergo torture for the shortfall. The summary does not specify whether coins are paid in this particular scenario beyond the general rule.
answers.evidence: Events — Harvest: pay one grain, cheese, or wine to Goods Market; if unable, pay 5 coins; if unable, torture. Wool and brocade are not food.

answers.answer: The neutral Scholar is lost from your bag and returns to its game-board supply, becoming recruitable again; its track marker does not move back. The colored starting Trader is kept, so no Follower is lost and no replacement draw is made.
answers.evidence: Events — Plague.

answers.answer: Pay the one available coin and replace each of the two missing coins with an eligible item: a built or unbuilt station; a random neutral Follower drawn only from your bag (return and redraw marked starting Followers); one Development Point moved left but never onto or past a coin space; one Goods Tile, Place Tile, or Technology tile. Surrendered items are removed from the game. Followers on Market or Action Spaces are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You cannot play an action that provides an unavailable Character, Technology, or Goods tile, even if another part would give a reward. It becomes available again when required stock returns, subject to normal requirements. If the common coin supply lacks enough coins, players cannot receive coins at that moment.
answers.evidence: Limited supplies.

answers.answer: A tie for most built stations awards the bonus Citizen to nobody. Goods score grain 1, cheese 2, wine 3, wool 4, brocade 5 each. Stations plus collected Citizens score (number of built stations + Citizens) × final Development Status. Tied scores go to the player furthest ahead on the Development Track; if still tied, victory is shared.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: Each player receives a board, bag, Merchant, 10 Trading Stations, 5 coins, 7 markers, and four marked starting Followers. Put starting Followers on the Market, Merchant in Orléans, and one marker on the first space of each of six Character Tracks and the Development Track. Keep coins and unbuilt stations in front of you. The youngest player takes Start Player.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2; Fewer players / Start Player.

answers.answer: Place 13 Citizens on their marked board/Deed spaces and set the remaining Citizen aside for the final station award. Put Technology in its supply and sort neutral Followers by profession into board buildings. Separate Place Tiles into categories I and II, inspectable at any time. In 4 players, shuffle map goods face down, deal one face up to every eligible Road/Waterway goods space, and sort remaining goods face up into Goods Market.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: 3 players: remove 2 neutral Farmers, Boatmen, Craftsmen, and Traders each; 3 neutral Knights, Scholars, and Monks each; remove 6 random goods; leave spaces marked 4 empty. 2 players: remove 4 of each first group; 6 of each second group; remove 12 random goods; leave spaces marked 3 or 4 empty. Remove all starting Followers of unused colors.
answers.evidence: Fewer players table and preceding sentence.

answers.answer: Farm House: Boatman + Craftsman. Village: Farmer + Boatman + Craftsman. University: Farmer + Craftsman + Trader. Castle: Farmer + Boatman + Trader. Monastery: Scholar + Trader.
answers.evidence: Actions table — required Followers.

answers.answer: Ship: Farmer + Boatman + Knight. Wagon: Farmer + Trader + Knight. Guildhall: Farmer + Craftsman + Knight.
answers.evidence: Actions table — required Followers.

answers.answer: Scriptorium requires Knight + Scholar. Town Hall requires one or two eligible Followers; its two spaces take neutral Followers, and the summary does not specify a printed profession restriction for Town Hall itself.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Scriptorium and Town Hall; Town Hall section says place one or two neutral Followers.

answers.answer: Yes. For each draw declined, you may move one Follower from an Action Space back to your Market. You may not move a Follower directly between Action Spaces.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers.

answers.answer: Yes. You may inspect your bag at any time, but must shuffle its contents afterward.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Followers.

answers.answer: Hour Glass → Census → Followers → Planning → Actions → Event → Start Player. Start Player passes left. Planning is simultaneous, with completion announced; if order matters, proceed clockwise from Start Player. Event payments and order-sensitive resolution also proceed clockwise from Start Player. Paid coins go to common supply; received coins come from it.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure phases 1–7.

answers.answer: Do not score immediately: finish the entire round in which the 18th tile is drawn, including its event, then proceed to final awards/scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions.

answers.answer: The player uniquely ahead on the Farmers Track gains the Census coin, regardless of how many Farmer tiles are in bags.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census.

answers.answer: Income pays coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: Events — Income.

answers.answer: Eight goods means two complete groups of three, so pay 2 coins; goods types do not affect the count. A shortfall causes torture.
answers.evidence: Events — Taxes: count all goods; pay 1 coin per complete group of 3 (round down); shortfall causes torture.

answers.answer: Receive 4 coins, one per built Trading Station; unbuilt reserve stations do not count.
answers.evidence: Events — Trading Day: 1 coin per built Trading Station.

answers.answer: Hayrick: Farmer, 1 grain; Cheese Factory: Farmer + Farmer, 1 cheese; Winery: Farmer + Trader, 1 wine; Wool Manufacturer: Boatman + Trader, 1 wool; Tailor Shop: Scholar + Trader, 1 brocade. Each takes the good from Goods Market and cannot be used if that good is absent there.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles; final goods-producing Place rule.

answers.answer: Shipping Line: Boatman, gain 1 Development Point. Brewery: Monk, gain 2 coins. Windmill: Craftsman + Craftsman, gain 2 coins and 1 Development Point. Library: Knight + Scholar, gain 2 Development Points.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles.

answers.answer: Any one Follower activates Pharmacy. Pay 1–3 coins, advancing one Development space per coin; paying two advances two spaces. Zero or four coins is not legal.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Pharmacy.

answers.answer: Cellar: Monk + Scholar, gain 4 coins. Office: Scholar + Scholar, gain 1 coin per built Trading Station. Hospital: Boatman + Scholar, gain coins equal to current Development Status.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles.

answers.answer: Horse Wagon requires Trader + Knight; it moves along one Road to an adjacent town and collects one good if available.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Horse Wagon.

answers.answer: Laboratory requires Scholar + Craftsman and gives a Technology tile subject to usual constraints. Your first Technology cannot be placed there because the first must replace a Farmer. A later Technology may be placed on either Laboratory space if no Technology is already there and normal constraints are met.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Laboratory; Technology.

answers.answer: Bathhouse requires Farmer. Draw 3 Followers from your bag, choose 2, and immediately place them on appropriate Action Spaces, not on the Bathhouse. Return the third drawn Follower and activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Bathhouse.

answers.answer: Place the one Follower you can legally place on an appropriate Action Space. Return the other two drawn Followers and the activating Bathhouse Follower to your bag. If none can be placed, return all three drawn Followers and the activating Follower to your bag.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Bathhouse: if only one or none can be placed, do so and return all other drawn Followers to bag.

answers.answer: It may be executed on a later action turn this round if you have not passed; the summary says the Place acquired and its abilities are immediately available, and actions are taken in freely chosen order during the Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Trader; Turn Structure — Actions.

answers.answer: Sacristy requires a Monk. If activated, during Phase 6 return its Monk to your bag instead of suffering a negative event such as Harvest, Taxes, or Plague.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Sacristy.

answers.answer: No. Pilgrimage prohibits Monk recruitment during Phase 5; this restriction applies before Phase 6, when Sacristy's event protection is used.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hour Glass; Sacristy; Events — Pilgrimage.

answers.answer: Herb Garden lets Boatmen replace Craftsmen, Traders, and Farmers on ordinary actions. It does not permit replacing Knights, Scholars, or Monks.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Herb Garden.

answers.answer: School lets Scholars replace other professions except Monks on ordinary actions. It has no activation cost; it is a passive ability. A Scholar cannot replace a required Monk.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — School; Monks.

answers.answer: No. Beneficial Deed spaces require exact depicted professions, so Herb Garden or School substitutions cannot fill a differently depicted Deed space. Gunpowder Tower also requires exact Deed types; using it does not change that.
answers.evidence: Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds; Gunpowder Tower row.

answers.answer: Gunpowder Tower adds 2 Market spaces. During Phase 3 place 1 or 2 drawn Followers there. In Planning, move one or both to Action Spaces; alternatively, in Actions send one or both directly to Beneficial Deeds in one action. Marked starting Followers cannot be sent, and Deeds require exact types.
answers.evidence: The 20 base Place Tiles — Gunpowder Tower.

answers.answer: The unique leader gains 1 coin; the two tied last players pay nothing.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Census: tied last place pays nothing.

answers.answer: After finishing round 18, before scoring, the unique leader in built Trading Stations takes the set-aside Citizen. It counts as a collected Citizen in final scoring.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: before scoring, unique most built stations takes Citizen; stations and collected Citizens are scored together.

answers.answer: Remove the lighter Pilgrimage tile, shuffle the other 17 Hour Glass tiles face down, then put Pilgrimage on top. In Phase 1, Start Player reveals the top tile.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4; Turn Structure — Hour Glass.

answers.answer: Each remaining coin scores 1 victory point.
answers.evidence: Scoring table — Coins.

answers.answer: Development Status starts at 1 and initial draw allowance is 4.
answers.evidence: Setup step 2.

answers.answer: Only lost Development Points can be regained. Surrendered goods, Followers, stations, Places, and Technology are removed from the game rather than returned to supplies.
answers.evidence: Torture (bankruptcy).

answers.answer: You may choose your actions' order freely.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Actions.

answers.answer: It is available immediately when acquired, including during the current Action Phase.
answers.evidence: Village recruitment — Trader: acquired Place and passive special ability are available immediately.

answers.answer: You may send just one or both; Town Hall accepts one or two eligible Followers in one action.
answers.evidence: Actions table — Town Hall; Town Hall and Beneficial Deeds.

answers.answer: You may take one good from the connection; the summary does not say taking it is mandatory, so you may leave it there.
answers.evidence: Movement and goods: “You may take one good” from the connection.

answers.answer: Yes. You may send the second on a later action turn in the same Action Phase before passing; Town Hall may send its Followers in separate action turns during that phase.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings — Town Hall in separate action turns.
